title: Physiotherapy for Patellar Tendinopathy – Progressive Tendon-Loading Exercise Therapy Combined with Hip and Core Exercises – An Additional Benefit?
summary: This study investigates a common knee problem called patellar tendon pain, which often affects athletes who jump frequently. The main question is whether adding specific exercises for the hip and core muscles to standard tendon-strengthening exercises helps reduce pain and improve knee function more than tendon exercises alone. Participants are divided into two groups: one does only the tendon exercises, the other also includes hip and core training. The study lasts six months, with regular check-ups to measure pain, function, strength, and knee stability.

interventions.name: Group A (control group): Participants receive a 6‑month standardized progressive tendon‑loading exercise (PTLE) program for the patellar tendon, including isometric, isotonic, plyometric and sport‑specific exercises, delivered via online videos and individually adapted to the pain level.
Group B (intervention group): Participants receive the same PTLE program as Group A, supplemented by specific hip and core stabilization exercises, also delivered via a protected online platform.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age 18-35 years, pain localized at the patellar tendon, especially during sports activity, tenderness on palpation at the inferior patella, VISA-P score below 80 points, physical ability to perform exercises and functional tests
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy, minor (under 18 years), underweight or overweight (BMI under 17 or over 35), acute knee or patellar tendon injuries, previous knee surgery without full rehabilitation, inflammatory joint diseases or familial hypercholesterolemia, use of medications affecting the patellar tendon (e.g., fluoroquinolones, corticosteroid injections) within the past 12 months, previous patellar tendon rupture, participation in other concurrent treatment programs, other knee conditions causing symptoms
